name: Hawking Radiation
statement: Quantum effects near a black hole's event horizon cause it to emit thermal radiation and slowly lose mass.
statementAccent: cause it to emit thermal radiation and slowly lose mass
meaning: Hawking radiation is a theoretical prediction that black holes are not perfectly black but emit a faint thermal glow due to quantum field effects in curved spacetime. Over immense timescales this radiation would cause a black hole to evaporate entirely.
mechanism: Near the event horizon, quantum vacuum fluctuations and the Unruh effect mean an accelerating observer experiences a thermal bath of particles; some pairs form such that one member escapes as outgoing radiation while its partner falls in, carrying away mass-energy and reducing the black hole’s mass over time.

examples.text: A solar-mass black hole would take roughly 10^67 years to fully evaporate via Hawking radiation, vastly longer than the current age of the universe, illustrating how faint the effect is for astrophysical black holes.

Researchers have reported observations of Hawking-radiation-like phenomena in "sonic black holes" made from Bose–Einstein condensates, where sound waves play the role of light near an analogue event horizon.
A 2010 laboratory experiment created an optical analogue of a white-hole event horizon reporting radiation resembling Hawking’s prediction, though its status as genuine confirmation remains disputed.

whyItMatters: Hawking radiation connects general relativity, quantum field theory, and thermodynamics, showing black holes have temperature and entropy, and it raises the black hole information paradox, a central open problem in theoretical physics.
limits: Hawking radiation has never been directly detected from an astrophysical black hole; only analogue laboratory systems have produced comparable effects, so its status for real black holes remains a theoretical, if widely accepted, prediction.
misreadings: It is often misdescribed simply as "particles escaping the black hole," which oversimplifies a subtler quantum field-theoretic effect involving vacuum fluctuations near the horizon rather than literal particle pairs splitting at a boundary.
origin: Predicted by Stephen Hawking in 1974, building on Jacob Bekenstein’s 1972 work relating black hole area to entropy.

sources.text: Hawking radiation, Wikipedia. — the 1974 prediction, the Unruh-effect mechanism, evaporation timescales, and the unresolved status of direct observation.
